thread:
anya: Customer reporting 400 from /v1/rerank for a large batch (500 items). They say it used to work.
marco: Can you paste the exact request and the error body?
anya: Minimal repro from their curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"meta":{"batch_id":"b-123","items":[{"id":"1","query":"q1","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"a"}]}]},"topk":"5"}'
```
anya: Response they get: `400 Bad Request` with body:
```
{"error":"invalid_request","message":"expected 'items' array at top level, got object"}
```
marco: Ah — payload is wrapped in `meta` and topk is a string. Our schema validator expects `items` at the root and topk as integer.
olivia: That wrapper was introduced by the customer's internal middleware, but interestingly the new JS SDK (v2.4.0) added an option to auto-wrap telemetry which can produce exactly this shape for some customers.
anya: Customer insists it was working last week. They upgraded SDK but forgot to mention. Repro steps they ran: send nested payload via HTTP proxy that sets `wrapTelemetry=true`.
marco: Two distinct validation failures then: 1) missing top-level `items` array, 2) `topk` type mismatch (string vs integer). Either can produce a 400.
dev-bot: [deploy] validation-service v1.12 returned validation error codes: INVALID_SCHEMA (code 4001), BAD_TYPE (code 4003).
olivia: Proposed immediate workaround for customer: send the nested `items` content as the request body root. Example fix:
```
// instead of sending { meta: { items: [...] }, topk: "5" }
// send:
{
  "items": [ /* same items array */ ],
  "topk": 5
}
```
anya: I pushed that to the customer, they tested, and it succeeded. They still want us to handle the wrapped shape gracefully since their proxy can't be changed quickly.
marco: Operational options: 1) Support can transform wrapped payloads in the proxy layer (quick but hacky), 2) Add a permissive parser that accepts `{meta:{items: [...]}}` for the rerank endpoint (safe if we log and warn), 3) Reject and document strictly.
olivia: I'll open an eng runtime ticket to add a compatibility shim with a feature flag. Ticket: RUNTIME-3247. Will include telemetry for how often wrapped payloads show up.
anya: Filed support ticket SR-78932 for the customer and noted workaround.
marco: Also found one more edge case — when candidates array is present but empty (`"candidates": []`) our service returns 400 because we require at least one candidate per item for rerank. Customer had this in a couple entries after a transformation step removed duplicates.
anya: Sent them a small script to filter out items with empty candidates before calling our API.
olivia: I'll add clearer docs note and an SDK validation error with a friendlier message: "each item must include non-empty candidates array".
marco: OK closing this Slack thread. Follow-ups: olivia will PR the shim (feature-flagged), I will update the KB with repro and the quick-fix script, anya will confirm customer is unblocked. :thumbsup:
anya: customer confirmed resolved, thanks everyone :relieved:
